q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Engine kilometres include train engine kilometres as well as shunting, light and other engine kilometres.
2. Shunting kilometres performed in yards are included in train kilometres.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: engine kilometres include train engine kilometres as well as shunting, light and other engine kilometres. Statement 2 is false: shunting kilometres performed in yards are not included in train kilometres.

q: The average number of passengers carried per train is computed as:

options.A: Number of passengers divided by the number of trains
options.B: Passenger kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres
options.C: Passenger earnings divided by passenger train kilometres
options.D: Seat kilometres divided by train kilometres

e: Average number of passengers carried per train = passenger kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres.

q: The average load of a loaded wagon is computed as:

options.A: Tonnes loaded divided by the number of wagons owned
options.B: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by total wagon kilometres
options.C: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by train kilometres
options.D: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by loaded wagon kilometres

e: Average load of a loaded wagon = Net Tonne Kilometres divided by loaded wagon kilometres.

q: Wagon kilometres per wagon day is an index which measures:

options.A: The average distance run by wagons per day, i.e. the utilisation of wagons in terms of distance
options.B: The average load carried by a wagon
options.C: The number of wagons repaired per day
options.D: The earnings per wagon per day

e: Wagon kilometres per wagon day measures the average distance run by wagons per day, i.e. the utilisation of wagons in terms of distance covered.

q: The utilisation of the goods carrying capacity offered is measured by the ratio of:

options.A: Gross Tonne Kilometres to Net Tonne Kilometres
options.C: Net Tonne Kilometres to the available tonne kilometres

e: Utilisation of the goods carrying capacity offered is measured by the ratio of Net Tonne Kilometres to the available tonne kilometres.

q: Where tickets issued by a station remain unaccounted for in the accounts rendered by it, the Traffic Accounts Office:

options.A: Ignores the omission till the annual inspection
options.B: Raises a debit against the station for the value of the unaccounted tickets
options.C: Cancels the entire ticket stock of the station
options.D: Recovers the amount from the passengers concerned

e: Where tickets issued by a station remain unaccounted for, the Traffic Accounts Office raises a debit against the station for the value of the unaccounted tickets.

q: Printed card tickets and blank paper tickets are supplied to stations:

options.A: By local purchase made by the Station Master
options.B: Free of accountal by the ticket printers
options.D: Against indents, and the accountal of the ticket stock is watched in the Traffic Accounts Office

e: Printed card tickets and blank paper tickets are supplied to stations against indents, and the accountal of the ticket stock is watched in the Traffic Accounts Office.

q: After computerisation of ticketing through PRS and UTS, the check of coaching earnings in the Traffic Accounts Office is exercised largely through:

options.A: Physical verification of every ticket at the stations
options.B: System-generated reports and exception statements thrown up by the computer systems
options.C: Inspection by the Railway Board's vigilance teams

e: After computerisation through PRS and UTS, the check of coaching earnings is exercised largely through system-generated reports and exception statements thrown up by the computer systems.

q: After computerisation of freight operations, the goods traffic and wagon-usage statistics are compiled mainly from the data captured in:
e: After computerisation of freight operations, goods traffic and wagon-usage statistics are compiled mainly from the data captured in FOIS.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Outward returns of goods traffic are rendered by the forwarding (booking) stations.
2. Inward returns of goods traffic are rendered by the destination stations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: outward returns of goods traffic are rendered by the forwarding (booking) stations, and inward returns are rendered by the destination stations.

q: Before goods delivered at a station are removed from the station premises:

options.A: No formality is required once the freight is paid
options.B: The goods are weighed again in the presence of the Station Master
options.C: The consignee must obtain a fresh Railway Receipt
options.D: Delivery is recorded in the delivery book and a gate pass is issued for their removal

e: Before goods are removed from station premises, delivery is recorded in the delivery book and a gate pass is issued for their removal.

q: A season ticket issued to a passenger entitles the holder to:

options.A: Unlimited journeys between the stations named on it during its period of validity
options.B: One journey in a month between any two stations in India
options.C: Travel only in unreserved suburban trains on a single day
options.D: A single return journey during its period of validity

e: A season ticket entitles the holder to unlimited journeys between the stations named on it during its period of validity.

q: In goods traffic, 'smalls' are:

options.A: Consignments booked at owner's risk only
options.C: Consignments which do not make up a full wagon load
options.D: Consignments of less than 10 kilograms in weight

e: In goods traffic, 'smalls' are consignments which do not make up a full wagon load.

q: When goods are booked at the owner's risk rate, the consignor is required to execute a:
e: When goods are booked at the owner's risk rate, the consignor is required to execute a Risk Note accepting the conditions of that rate.

q: Traffic costing on Indian Railways compiles unit costs such as:

options.D: Cost per train kilometre, cost per Net Tonne Kilometre and cost per passenger kilometre

e: Traffic costing compiles unit costs such as cost per train kilometre, cost per Net Tonne Kilometre and cost per passenger kilometre for the different services.

q: In traffic costing, 'line haul cost' means:

options.A: The cost of hauling traffic between terminals, excluding the costs incurred at terminals/stations
options.B: The total cost of a service including all terminal costs
options.C: The cost of construction of the railway line
options.D: The cost of train crew only

e: Line haul cost means the cost of hauling traffic between terminals, excluding the costs incurred at terminals and stations.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fully distributed cost allocates the fixed and overhead costs also to the individual services.
2. Marginal (variable) cost takes into account only those costs which vary with the volume of traffic.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: fully distributed cost allocates fixed and overhead costs also to individual services, while marginal (variable) cost takes only those costs which vary with the volume of traffic.

q: Wharfage or demurrage accrued at a station can be waived or remitted only:

options.A: By the goods clerk on duty
options.B: Under the orders of the competent authority, in exercise of the powers delegated for the purpose
options.C: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.D: By the consignee on payment of a fee

e: Wharfage or demurrage accrued at a station can be waived or remitted only under the orders of the competent authority, in exercise of the powers delegated for the purpose.

q: Contracts for parking, advertisement and similar commercial activities at stations, which yield non-fare earnings, are awarded through:

options.B: Selection by the staff welfare committee

e: Contracts for parking, advertisement and similar commercial activities at stations, which yield non-fare earnings, are awarded through the prescribed tender or e-auction process.

q: At junction (interchange) points between zonal railways, the wagons and vehicles handed over and received are recorded, and these records form the basis of:

options.A: Wagon-usage and interchange statistics between the railways
options.B: The pay bills of the junction staff

e: At junction interchange points, the records of wagons and vehicles handed over and received form the basis of wagon-usage and interchange statistics between the railways.

q: The abbreviation TAMS, used in the Traffic Accounts Offices, stands for:
e: TAMS stands for Traffic Accounts Management System, the system used in the Traffic Accounts Offices.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the Unreserved Ticketing System (UTS), unreserved ticket sales are recorded system-wise for each booking window/shift.
2. The system-generated summaries of UTS sales are used in the Traffic Accounts Office for checking the coaching earnings of stations.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: under UTS, unreserved ticket sales are recorded system-wise for each booking window or shift, and the system-generated summaries are used in the Traffic Accounts Office for checking stations' coaching earnings.

q: 'Coaching outstandings' at a station broadly represent:

options.A: The cash held in the station safe
options.C: Salary dues of the booking staff
options.D: The value of tickets and Excess Fare Tickets issued but not accounted for or remitted, recoverable from the station

e: Coaching outstandings at a station represent the value of tickets and Excess Fare Tickets issued but not accounted for or remitted, recoverable from the station.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the accounts rendered by a goods shed?

options.B: Wharfage and demurrage accrued and collected
options.C: Record of goods delivered and gate passes issued
options.D: Pay and allowances of the goods shed staff

e: Pay and allowances of the goods shed staff are establishment expenditure and do not form part of the accounts rendered by a goods shed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transhipment of goods becomes necessary at break-of-gauge points, where traffic passes from one gauge to another.
2. Transhipment en route on account of a wagon becoming unfit (sick wagon) is carried out at railway cost and no charge is recovered from the consignee for it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: transhipment is necessary at break-of-gauge points where traffic passes from one gauge to another, and transhipment due to a sick wagon en route is done at railway cost with no charge to the consignee.

q: The cost of transhipping through-booked goods at a break-of-gauge point is:

options.A: Recovered from the consignor in addition to the freight
options.B: Shared equally between the consignor and the consignee
options.C: Recovered from the consignee before delivery
options.D: Borne by the Railways as part of the through carriage

e: The cost of transhipping through-booked goods at a break-of-gauge point is borne by the Railways as part of the through carriage, and is not recovered from the parties.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Repacking of a consignment is undertaken en route or at destination when its packing is found damaged or defective, so that the goods can be carried and delivered safely.
2. Where repacking is necessitated by the defective packing provided by the consignor, the repacking charges are recoverable from the party.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: repacking is undertaken when packing is found damaged or defective so the goods can be carried and delivered safely, and where the consignor's defective packing caused it, the charges are recoverable from the party.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where repacking becomes necessary because the goods were damaged by railway handling, the repacking charges are recovered from the consignee.
2. Repacking charges leviable from a party are collected before the goods are delivered.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: where repacking is needed because goods were damaged by railway handling, the charges are borne by the Railways, not recovered from the consignee. Statement 2 is true: repacking charges leviable from a party are collected before delivery.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A wagon found overloaded on weighment is charged for the excess weight loaded beyond the permissible carrying capacity.
2. Overloading charges so recovered form part of the goods earnings.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: a wagon found overloaded on weighment is charged for the excess weight beyond the permissible carrying capacity, and the overloading charges so recovered form part of goods earnings.

q: Overloading of wagons is detected primarily through:

options.A: Visual estimation by the goods clerk
options.B: The declaration of the consignor alone
options.C: Weighment on weighbridges en route or at destination
options.D: The monthly statement of the Travelling Inspector of Accounts

e: Overloading of wagons is detected primarily through weighment on weighbridges en route or at destination.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Powers to waive demurrage and wharfage are delegated in graded monetary slabs, so that larger amounts can be waived only by higher authorities.
2. The station official who levied the demurrage can himself waive it in all cases.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: powers to waive demurrage and wharfage are delegated in graded monetary slabs, larger amounts being waivable only by higher authorities. Statement 2 is false: the official who levied the charge cannot himself waive it in all cases.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Waiver of demurrage/wharfage relieves the party of charges which have accrued but have not yet been paid.
2. Refund of demurrage/wharfage means repayment of charges which have already been collected.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: waiver of demurrage or wharfage relieves the party of charges which have accrued but not yet been paid, while refund means repayment of charges already collected.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An 'unconnected' consignment is one received at the destination without the corresponding booking particulars/invoice, so that it cannot immediately be connected with its booking.
2. An 'unclaimed' consignment is one which the consignee fails to take delivery of within the prescribed time after its arrival.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: an unconnected consignment is received without the corresponding booking particulars or invoice so it cannot immediately be connected with its booking, and an unclaimed consignment is one whose delivery is not taken within the prescribed time after arrival.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Unclaimed consignments are destroyed after the expiry of the prescribed period.
2. Unclaimed consignments are disposed of by public auction after due notice, and the sale proceeds are applied first towards the dues of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: unclaimed consignments are not destroyed. Statement 2 is true: they are disposed of by public auction after due notice, and the sale proceeds are applied first towards the dues of the Railways.

q: Unconnected consignments received at a station are:

options.C: Returned to the forwarding station without any record
options.D: Entered in a register and kept under watch while efforts are made to connect them with their booking particulars, failing which they are dealt with as unclaimed consignments

e: Unconnected consignments are entered in a register and kept under watch while efforts are made to connect them with their booking particulars, failing which they are dealt with as unclaimed consignments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Perishable consignments remaining unclaimed must be retained for the full prescribed period before they can be disposed of.
2. The disposal of unclaimed consignments is effected by public auction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: perishable consignments need not be retained for the full prescribed period before disposal. Statement 2 is true: disposal of unclaimed consignments is effected by public auction.

q: Where the Railway Receipt is lost or is not forthcoming, delivery of a consignment may be given:

options.B: Only after the expiry of one year
options.C: Only after the goods are auctioned
options.D: Against an indemnity bond executed by the claimant

e: Where the Railway Receipt is lost or not forthcoming, delivery of the consignment may be given against an indemnity bond executed by the claimant.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every remittance of cash from a station to the cash office/bank is accompanied by a cash remittance note.
2. Credits for station remittances are afforded in the accounts solely on the basis of the station's own statement, without any acknowledgement of the bank or the cash office.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: every remittance of cash from a station is accompanied by a cash remittance note. Statement 2 is false: credits are afforded on the acknowledgement of the bank or cash office, not solely on the station's own statement.

q: The traffic Cash Office is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Receiving remittances from stations, depositing the cash into the bank and accounting for the same

e: The traffic Cash Office is primarily responsible for receiving remittances from stations, depositing the cash into the bank and accounting for the same.

q: Amounts realised by ticket checking staff through Excess Fare Tickets during their duty are:

options.A: Retained by them till the end of the month
options.B: Remitted directly to the Railway Board
options.C: Credited to the staff welfare fund
options.D: Deposited with the station/cash office on completion of duty and accounted for in the station accounts

e: Amounts realised through Excess Fare Tickets are deposited with the station or cash office on completion of duty and accounted for in the station accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Excess Fare Ticket books issued to ticket checking staff are accounted for as valuable documents and all the foils must be duly accounted for.
2. The amounts shown as collected in the Excess Fare Tickets are deposited by the staff at the end of the month only.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: EFT books issued to ticket checking staff are accounted for as valuable documents and all foils must be duly accounted for. Statement 2 is false: collections are deposited on completion of duty, not only at the end of the month.

q: The fare and excess charge realised by ticket checking staff from passengers travelling without proper tickets are credited to:
e: The fare and excess charge realised by ticket checking staff from passengers travelling without proper tickets are credited to coaching earnings.

q: A passenger found travelling in a higher class than the one for which he holds a ticket is realised, by the ticket checking staff:

options.A: The full fare of the higher class afresh
options.C: A fixed penalty irrespective of the distance travelled
options.D: The difference of fare between the class held and the class travelled in, together with the excess charge

e: A passenger travelling in a higher class than his ticket is realised the difference of fare between the class held and the class travelled in, together with the excess charge.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a departmental catering unit, the sale proceeds are receipts of the Railways.
2. In a licensed catering unit, the sale proceeds belong to the licensee and only the licence fee is an earning of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: in a departmental catering unit the sale proceeds are receipts of the Railways, while in a licensed unit the proceeds belong to the licensee and only the licence fee is a railway earning.

q: In respect of catering and other commercial contracts, the Traffic Accounts Office ensures that:

options.A: The menus of the catering units are approved by it
options.B: The staff of the units are posted by the Accounts Department
options.C: The raw material for the units is purchased centrally
options.D: The licence fees and other dues recoverable under the contracts are fully recovered and brought to account

e: In respect of catering and other commercial contracts, the Traffic Accounts Office ensures that the licence fees and other dues recoverable under the contracts are fully recovered and brought to account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Earnings from advertisements and commercial publicity are accounted under Sundry Other Earnings.
2. Such earnings are apportioned among the zonal railways on the basis of distance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: earnings from advertisements and commercial publicity are accounted under Sundry Other Earnings. Statement 2 is false: sundry earnings are not apportioned among zonal railways.

q: Which of the following is NOT a source of sundry (non-fare) earnings of the Railways?
e: Passenger fares are coaching earnings, not a source of sundry (non-fare) earnings; parking, land licensing and advertisement contracts are non-fare sources.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Licence fee received for the use of railway land is accounted as a goods earning.
2. A licence of railway land gives the licensee only a permission to use the land and does not create any tenancy or leasehold interest in his favour.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: licence fee for railway land is a sundry earning, not a goods earning. Statement 2 is true: a licence only permits use of the land and creates no tenancy or leasehold interest in the licensee's favour.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Licence fee for railway land is normally recovered in advance for the licence period.
2. Unauthorised occupation of railway land is regularised automatically on payment of the normal licence fee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: licence fee for railway land is normally recovered in advance for the licence period. Statement 2 is false: unauthorised occupation is not regularised automatically merely on payment of the normal licence fee.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Goods outstandings at a station include 'to-pay' freight which has not yet been collected.
2. Goods outstandings also include wharfage and demurrage which have accrued but have not yet been realised.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: goods outstandings at a station include 'to-pay' freight not yet collected, and also wharfage and demurrage which have accrued but have not yet been realised.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Items held under suspense in the station accounts can be written off by the station itself at the close of the financial year.
2. Suspense items in station accounts remain under watch until they are cleared with supporting particulars in the subsequent accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: a station cannot write off its own suspense items; write-off needs the sanction of the competent authority. Statement 2 is true: suspense debits stay under watch until cleared with supporting particulars in subsequent accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Coaching outstandings and goods outstandings of stations are watched separately in the Traffic Accounts Office.
2. Station outstandings represent amounts recoverable from the stations and are reflected in the Accounts Office Balance Sheet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: coaching and goods outstandings are watched separately in the Traffic Accounts Office, and station outstandings, being amounts recoverable from stations, are reflected in the Accounts Office Balance Sheet.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The approximate earnings figures issued every ten days are compiled after full internal check of station accounts by the Traffic Accounts Office.
2. The earnings finally brought to account are reconciled with the approximate/statistical figures and the differences are investigated and settled.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: the ten-day approximate earnings are compiled from stations' approximate reports before any full internal check. Statement 2 is true: earnings finally brought to account are reconciled with the approximate figures and differences investigated and settled.

q: The monthly reconciliation of earnings between the Commercial and Accounts departments is carried out primarily to:

options.A: Agree the statistical (approximate) earnings with the earnings actually brought to account and to investigate the differences
options.B: Fix the earnings targets for the next month
options.C: Allot rakes and wagons to divisions
options.D: Decide the postings of commercial staff

e: The monthly Commercial-Accounts reconciliation exists to agree the statistical (approximate) earnings with the earnings actually brought to account, so that differences between the two sets of figures are investigated and settled.

q: The final monthly earnings of a zonal railway for accounts purposes are:

options.A: The approximate figures issued every ten days
options.B: The figures furnished by stations without any check
options.C: The Budget Estimates of earnings for the month
options.D: The earnings brought to account by the Traffic Accounts Office after internal check

e: The final monthly earnings are those brought to account by the Traffic Accounts Office after internal check of the station returns; the ten-day approximate figures are only provisional and are superseded by the accounted figures.

q: The average rate realised per tonne kilometre of goods traffic is computed as:

options.A: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried
options.B: Goods earnings divided by tonnes originated
options.C: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by wagon kilometres
options.D: Goods earnings divided by Net Tonne Kilometres

e: Average rate per tonne kilometre = goods earnings divided by Net Tonne Kilometres. It measures the average realisation for moving one tonne of goods over one kilometre.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dividend payable on the capital-at-charge is included in the working expenses for computing the Operating Ratio.
2. The Operating Ratio improves when the gross earnings grow at a faster rate than the working expenses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: dividend on capital-at-charge is paid out of net revenue and is not a working expense, so it is excluded from the Operating Ratio. Statement 2 is true: the ratio improves when earnings grow faster than working expenses.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cost per Net Tonne Kilometre is worked out by dividing the total cost of the goods services by the Net Tonne Kilometres performed.
2. A comparison of the earnings per Net Tonne Kilometre with the cost per Net Tonne Kilometre indicates whether the goods traffic is, on the average, remunerative.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: cost per Net Tonne Kilometre is the total cost of goods services divided by the Net Tonne Kilometres performed, and comparing it with earnings per Net Tonne Kilometre shows whether goods traffic is remunerative on the average.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Net revenue is the excess of gross earnings over the capital expenditure of the year.
2. Return on capital is the net revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: net revenue is the excess of gross earnings over working expenses, not over capital expenditure. Statement 2 is true: return on capital is net revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge.

q: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day is an index of:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day measures the goods output obtained from each locomotive per day, so it is an index of locomotive utilisation on goods services.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Wagons under and awaiting repair are excluded from the effective wagon fleet.
2. Indices based on wagon days, such as Net Tonne Kilometres per wagon day, are computed with reference to the total wagon fleet including wagons under repair.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is true: wagons under or awaiting repair are not available for traffic and are excluded from the effective fleet. Statement 2 is false: wagon-day indices are computed on the effective fleet, not the total fleet including wagons under repair.

q:
Consider the following statements about Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevaks (JTBS):
1. The sevaks earn a commission on the tickets sold by them, while the fare collected is an earning (coaching) of the Railways.
2. The sevaks are authorised agents who sell unreserved tickets from premises outside the station.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: JTBS are authorised agents selling unreserved tickets from premises outside stations; the fare collected is a coaching earning of the Railways, while the sevak earns only the prescribed commission on sales.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The fares collected by IRCTC for e-tickets are the earnings of IRCTC and are not remitted to the Railways.
2. The fare amounts on e-tickets are settled with the Railways and are accounted as coaching earnings after reconciliation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is false: e-ticket fares belong to the Railways, not IRCTC; only the convenience fee is IRCTC's. Statement 2 is true: the fare amounts are settled with the Railways and accounted as coaching earnings after reconciliation.

q: Wharfage and demurrage charges which have accrued at a station but have not been collected by the end of the month are:

options.A: Brought to account in the station accounts on accrual and shown as outstanding till realised
options.B: Ignored till they are actually collected
options.C: Accounted only in the annual accounts

e: Wharfage and demurrage accrued but not collected are brought to account on the accrual basis in the month they accrue and shown as outstanding in the station accounts until realised.

q: The statistical statements of a zonal railway are compiled mainly from:

options.A: The returns and statements rendered by the stations and operating units
options.C: The Budget documents of the Railway Board
options.D: The inspection reports of the audit department

e: Zonal railway statistics are compiled mainly from the returns and statements rendered by stations and operating units, which record the traffic actually handled and the services performed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Local traffic is traffic which both originates and terminates on the same railway.
2. Through traffic is traffic which is carried over two or more railways during its journey.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both definitions are correct: local traffic both originates and terminates on the same railway, while through traffic is carried over two or more railways during its journey.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Tonnes originating' are the tonnes of goods booked (loaded) at the stations of the railway.
2. 'Tonnes carried' by a railway comprise its originating tonnes plus the tonnes received by it from other railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: tonnes originating are the tonnes booked and loaded at the railway's own stations, and tonnes carried comprise those originating tonnes plus the tonnes received from other railways.

q: 'Vehicle kilometres' in coaching statistics represent:

options.A: The total distance run by locomotives hauling coaching trains
options.B: The aggregate distance run by all coaching vehicles (coaches)
options.C: The total distance run by empty coaches only
options.D: The route kilometres over which coaching services are provided

e: Vehicle kilometres are the aggregate distance run by all coaching vehicles (coaches); they measure coaching vehicle utilisation, unlike train kilometres, which count the run of the train as a whole.

q: 'Seat kilometres offered' are computed as:

options.A: The seating capacity of the vehicles multiplied by the vehicle kilometres run, aggregated over all services
options.B: The number of passengers multiplied by the average journey length
options.C: The number of seats multiplied by the number of trains run
options.D: The passenger kilometres divided by the load factor

e: Seat kilometres offered = seating capacity of the vehicles multiplied by the vehicle kilometres run, aggregated over all services. It represents the total carrying capacity (supply) offered to passengers.

q: 'Available tonne kilometres' in goods statistics represent:

options.A: The Net Tonne Kilometres actually performed during the period
options.B: The Gross Tonne Kilometres performed by goods trains
options.C: The sum, over all loaded wagons, of the carrying capacity of each wagon multiplied by the distance it runs loaded
options.D: The tonnes carried multiplied by the route kilometres of the railway

e: Available tonne kilometres represent the capacity offered: for each loaded wagon, its carrying capacity is multiplied by the distance it runs loaded, and the results are summed. Unlike Net Tonne Kilometres, they use capacity, not actual load.

q: The average gross load of goods trains is computed as:

options.A: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by route kilometres
options.B: Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres
options.C: Tonnes carried divided by the number of wagons loaded
options.D: Net Tonne Kilometres divided by wagon kilometres

e: Average gross load of goods trains = Gross Tonne Kilometres divided by goods train kilometres. GTKM includes the tare weight of wagons, so this gives the average gross trailing load per train.

q: A 'wagon day' in railway statistics means:

options.A: One wagon on line (available for use) for a period of 24 hours
options.B: One wagon loaded during a calendar day
options.C: One wagon detained at a station for loading
options.D: The day on which a wagon is sent to the workshop for repair

e: A wagon day means one wagon on line, that is available for use, for a period of 24 hours; wagon-day totals are the base for indices of wagon utilisation.

q: The average rate realised per passenger kilometre is computed as:

options.A: Passenger earnings divided by the number of passengers carried
options.B: Coaching earnings divided by train kilometres
options.C: Passenger kilometres divided by passenger earnings
options.D: Passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres

e: Average rate realised per passenger kilometre = passenger earnings divided by passenger kilometres. It shows the average fare realisation for carrying one passenger over one kilometre.

q: The density of passenger traffic on a section is expressed as:
e: Density of passenger traffic expresses how intensively the network is used for passenger traffic and is measured as passenger kilometres performed per route kilometre.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Detention of wagons at loading and unloading points and at terminals increases the wagon turn-round.
2. A smaller wagon turn-round figure indicates better utilisation of the wagon fleet.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: detentions at loading and unloading points and at terminals lengthen the time a wagon takes to complete its cycle, increasing turn-round; a smaller turn-round means wagons are released and reused faster, indicating better utilisation.

q: Passenger fares for through journeys on Indian Railways are charged on the 'telescopic' principle, which means that:

options.A: The fare is the sum of the separate fares for each railway over which the journey is performed
options.B: The rate per kilometre decreases as the distance of the journey increases, so that the through fare is less than the sum of the fares for its parts
options.C: A flat fare is charged irrespective of the distance travelled
options.D: The fare increases in direct proportion to the square of the distance

e: Under the telescopic principle, the rate per kilometre decreases as the distance increases, so the through fare for the whole journey is less than the sum of the separate fares for its parts.

q: A passenger holding an RAC (Reservation Against Cancellation) ticket is entitled to:

options.A: Sitting accommodation in the reserved coach, with a berth being allotted to him as and when a vacancy arises on cancellation
options.B: A confirmed berth in a higher class
options.C: A full refund of fare at the destination station
options.D: Travel in any train on the same day without further charge

e: An RAC ticket entitles the passenger to sitting accommodation in the reserved coach, and a berth is allotted to him as and when a vacancy arises through cancellation.

q: In railway reservation, the abbreviation PNR stands for:
e: PNR stands for Passenger Name Record; it is the unique record, identified by a ten-digit number, under which a reserved booking is stored in the reservation system.

q: In the case of a confirmed Premium Tatkal ticket, the position regarding refund on cancellation is that:

options.A: Full fare is refunded without any deduction
options.B: Fare is refunded after deduction of clerkage charges only
options.C: Fifty per cent of the fare is refunded
options.D: No refund is admissible on cancellation of the ticket

e: No refund is admissible on cancellation of a confirmed Premium Tatkal ticket; the premium tatkal fare, once booked and confirmed, is forfeited on cancellation by the passenger.

q: The 'Vikalp' scheme of Indian Railways relates to:

options.A: Allotment of lower berths to senior citizens
options.B: Booking of tickets under the emergency quota
options.C: Change of the boarding station by a passenger
options.D: Allotment of accommodation in an alternate train to waitlisted passengers who have opted for the scheme

e: Vikalp is the scheme under which a waitlisted passenger who opts for it can be allotted accommodation in an alternate train, including trains departing later, if a berth becomes available.

q: In connection with unreserved ticketing, the abbreviation ATVM stands for:
e: ATVM stands for Automatic Ticket Vending Machine, the self-service machines installed at stations for issuing unreserved tickets, typically using smart cards.

q: Where a train is fully cancelled by the Railways, the passengers holding tickets for that train are entitled to:

options.A: Refund of fare after deduction of the prescribed cancellation charge
options.B: Full refund of fare without deduction of any cancellation charge
options.C: Refund of only fifty per cent of the fare
options.D: No refund, but free rebooking on any future date

e: Where the Railways themselves fully cancel a train, the passenger is entitled to a full refund of fare without deduction of any cancellation charge, since the cancellation is not of his making.

q: A passenger who travels in a lower class than the class for which he holds a reserved ticket is entitled to:

options.B: Refund of the full fare of the higher class
options.C: A berth in the higher class in the next train
options.D: Refund of the difference of fare between the two classes, claimed on the basis of the certificate issued by the ticket checking staff

e: A passenger who travels in a lower class than booked is entitled to a refund of the difference of fare between the two classes, claimed on the basis of the certificate issued by the ticket checking staff.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A season ticket is issued in the name of a particular holder and is not transferable.
2. If a season ticket is used by a person other than its holder, the ticket is liable to be forfeited and the user treated as travelling without a proper ticket.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: a season ticket is issued in the named holder's favour and is not transferable; if used by another person, it is liable to forfeiture and the user is treated as travelling without a proper ticket.

q: Luggage carried by a passenger in excess of the free allowance admissible to him:

options.A: Is carried free up to twice the free allowance
options.B: Is charged at the goods (freight) rates
options.C: Is charged as parcel traffic at parcel rates
options.D: Must be booked and is charged at the prescribed luggage rates

e: Luggage in excess of the free allowance must be booked and is charged at the prescribed luggage rates; it is neither carried free nor charged at parcel or freight rates.

q: In goods booking, the 'chargeable weight' of a consignment means:

options.A: The weight as declared by the consignor, in all cases
options.B: The actual weight of the consignment or the minimum weight condition prescribed for the wagon/class of traffic, whichever is higher
options.C: The carrying capacity of the wagon used, in all cases
options.D: The average weight of similar consignments booked at the station

e: Chargeable weight is the actual weight of the consignment or the minimum weight condition prescribed for the wagon or class of traffic, whichever is higher, so that the minimum chargeable load is always recovered.

q: The 'percentage charge' levied in connection with goods booking is charged:

options.A: On all consignments booked at owner's risk
options.B: On the freight charges, as a surcharge during the busy season
options.C: On every Railway Receipt issued at the forwarding station
options.D: On the value declared by the consignor in excess of the prescribed limit, when the goods are booked at railway risk, towards the enhanced liability of the Railways

e: The percentage charge is levied on the value declared by the consignor in excess of the prescribed limit when goods are booked at railway risk; it pays for the Railways' enhanced liability on the higher declared value.

q: The remark 'said to contain' endorsed on a Railway Receipt signifies that:

options.A: The goods were packed and loaded by the consignor and their contents were not checked by the railway staff
options.B: The goods are of a perishable nature
options.C: The freight on the consignment has not been paid
options.D: The consignment is booked at railway risk

e: 'Said to contain' means the consignment was packed and loaded by the consignor and its contents were not verified by railway staff, so the Railways do not vouch for the contents as booked.

q: The endorsement 'sender's weight accepted' on a Railway Receipt indicates that:

options.A: The consignment was weighed on the railway weighbridge at the forwarding station
options.B: The overloading charges have been accepted by the sender
options.C: The weight of the consignment can never be questioned thereafter
options.D: The weight declared by the consignor has been accepted for booking as no weighbridge is available at the forwarding station, subject to weighment en route or at destination

e: 'Sender's weight accepted' records that the consignor's declared weight was accepted because no weighbridge is available at the forwarding station, subject to weighment en route or at destination.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Copies of the goods invoice are prepared at the forwarding station and a copy accompanies the consignment to the destination station.
2. The destination station tallies the consignment with the invoice particulars at the time of delivery and compiles its inward returns from the invoices received.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: invoice copies are prepared at the forwarding station and one copy travels with the consignment; the destination station tallies the consignment with the invoice at delivery and compiles its inward returns from the invoices received.

q: 'Open delivery' of a consignment is granted when:

options.A: The consignee asks for delivery on a holiday
options.B: The Railway Receipt is surrendered after the expiry of the free time
options.C: The consignment has arrived in a damaged condition or short, and the extent of the damage or shortage is assessed in the presence of railway officials before delivery is taken
options.D: The consignment is booked on a 'to-pay' basis

e: Open delivery is granted when a consignment arrives damaged or short: the extent of damage or shortage is assessed in the presence of railway officials before the consignee takes delivery, protecting his claim.

q: A 'shortage certificate' in goods traffic is:

options.A: Issued by the destination station to the consignee where the consignment is delivered short of the booked quantity or weight, in support of his claim
options.B: Issued by the forwarding station when a wagon is not supplied in time
options.C: Issued by the Traffic Accounts Office when freight is undercharged
options.D: Issued by the claims office when a claim is repudiated

e: A shortage certificate is issued by the destination station to the consignee where the consignment is delivered short of the booked quantity or weight; it supports his claim for compensation.

q: 'Diversion' of a goods consignment means:

options.A: Carriage of the consignment by a longer route for operational reasons
options.B: Transfer of the consignment from one wagon to another en route
options.C: Disposal of the consignment by auction at an intermediate station
options.D: Change of the destination of a consignment in transit, made on the request of the consignor or the holder of the Railway Receipt on payment of the prescribed charges

e: Diversion means changing the destination of a consignment while it is in transit, done on the request of the consignor or the Railway Receipt holder on payment of the prescribed charges.

q: Stores and materials carried over the Railways for the Railways' own use are booked:

options.A: On Railway Material Consignment (RMC) notes, and the freight is accounted for by adjustment, no cash freight being collected
options.B: On ordinary Railway Receipts against payment of freight in cash
options.C: Free of all accountal, without any document
options.D: On parcel way bills at parcel rates

e: Stores and materials carried for the Railways' own use are booked on Railway Material Consignment (RMC) notes; no cash freight is collected and the freight is accounted for by book adjustment.

q: The haulage charges for the movement of container trains over the railway network are paid to the Indian Railways by:
e: CONCOR operates the container trains and pays haulage charges to Indian Railways for hauling them over the railway network.

q: In respect of leasing of parcel space in trains:

options.A: The lease charges recovered from the operators belong to the station staff welfare fund
options.B: The parcel space in trains can be leased only to State Governments
options.C: The leasing is done without any contract or agreement
options.D: Parcel space in brake/luggage vans (SLR) and parcel vans is leased out to private operators under contract, and the lease charges so recovered are earnings of the Railways

e: Parcel space in brake/luggage vans (SLR) and parcel vans is leased to private operators under contract, and the lease charges recovered are earnings of the Railways.

q: Receipts from cloak rooms and retiring rooms at stations are classified under:
e: Receipts from cloak rooms and retiring rooms are classified under Sundry other earnings, as they are miscellaneous station receipts not forming part of coaching, goods or other coaching earnings.

q: 'Way leave' charges recovered by the Railways are charges for:

options.A: Permission to lay cables, pipelines and similar facilities across or along railway land and premises
options.B: Leave granted to railway staff for way-side stations
options.C: Detention of wagons at wayside stations
options.D: Use of the railway siding by private parties

e: Way leave charges are recovered for granting permission to lay cables, pipelines and similar facilities across or along railway land and premises.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Free time' is the period allowed free of charge for the loading or unloading of wagons and for the removal of goods from the station premises.
2. Demurrage accrues for detention of wagons beyond the free time, and wharfage for non-removal of goods beyond the free time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both are true: free time is the period allowed free for loading or unloading wagons and for removing goods; detention of wagons beyond free time attracts demurrage, and non-removal of goods beyond free time attracts wharfage.

q: In the apportionment of earnings of through traffic, the amount first set apart for the railways performing the terminal (loading/unloading) services, before the balance is divided in proportion to the distance carried, represents:
e: In apportioning through-traffic earnings, terminal charges are first set apart for the railways performing the loading and unloading (terminal) services; only the balance is divided among the railways in proportion to distance carried.
